title: Re-roll: choose the visual world for the cliproxy panel
question: A fresh hand; every earlier direction is out. Each card is one world for every page (Overview, Accounts, API keys, Models, Usage, Settings), shown on the Overview.

options.label: Munich ’72 system
options.lineage: Otl Aicher’s identity program for the 1972 Munich Games
options.thesis: An identity program instead of a dashboard theme: every provider, page and state has a fixed mark and colour in one strict system.
materials: Paper ground, sky-blue rail, meadow green for healthy, silver for idle, navy ink instead of black, orange for attention; red only for failures
One grotesk family (Hanken Grotesk, Univers in spirit) with tabular figures; sentence-case headings, no all-caps eyebrows, no mono labels
Provider and state pictograms drawn on one circle-and-45° construction grid
options.viewport: Sky-blue rail with page pictograms. Top: one orange band listing what needs attention (the only reversed plate on the screen). Below: account quota rows on one shared 0–100% scale (5-hour and weekly windows, reset time) beside a 24-hour traffic chart of requests, failures and tokens. Every account, model and key name links to its page.
options.risk: The pastel spectrum can read soft or sporty; it stays crisp only through navy ink, the strict grid and pictograms legible at 16 px.

raised.raise: Columns never move; only values change, and a state change restyles its row without breaking the grid.
Exactly one item per screen reverses out: the most urgent thing, navy on orange.
Flat, unmodulated colour everywhere: no gradients, glows or drop shadows.
Every account, model and key name is a link to its one home; a usage row jumps straight to its account.

regions.label: account quota rows, one shared scale

options.label: Utility statement
options.lineage: gas and electric statements: usage against allowance, history bars, the due date
options.thesis: Each account reads like a meter statement: this period’s use against its allowance, the past periods beside it, and the date it resets.
materials: Statement white, utility blue header band, allowance grey, ink; amber near the limit, red when cut off
Public Sans throughout, figures tabular and right-aligned
options.viewport: Utility-blue header with the page tabs. Each account is a statement block: a large 'resets in 2 h 35 m' box, use this window against the allowance, a 12-bar history of past windows with this one highlighted, and last-period comparison. A charges table underneath breaks tokens down by model.
options.risk: The most literal reading of 'quota = bill', and close to every billing dashboard; the fixed statement layout can feel bureaucratic.

regions.label: Claude statement: use vs allowance, resets in

options.label: Reference manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with coloured tab dividers and acetate overlays
options.thesis: The panel as the gateway’s manual: each section owns one full-strength hue, and a stepped tab rail shows the whole book at once.
materials: Milky leaves over a divider board in the section’s hue; vermilion held back for errors
A grotesk for data and headings, a book serif only for help text
Changes step in 90 ms, no easing
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the right edge, one tab per page, sized by how much it holds; the current page’s hue fills the board behind milky content leaves: attention list, account quotas, traffic.
options.case: Holds audience identification (the operator’s developer world grew up on manuals like this); loses product clarity, because translucent leaves over strong colour cost contrast in dense tables.
options.risk: Full-strength hues behind tables tire the eye, and the stepped motion can feel abrupt.

options.label: High-density modules
options.thesis: The whole gateway on one screen: a mosaic of ruled modules, each headed by a small tab.
materials: Hairline-ruled modules packed edge to edge; tabs moved from utility red to indigo so red stays for failures
A compact gothic sans at small sizes, tight leading
Hover raises a module’s border and reveals its actions
options.viewport: A multi-row top nav; below, a dense grid of modules: attention, each account’s quota, traffic, top models, recent failures, config warnings, all visible without scrolling.
options.case: Holds product clarity (everything at once suits a weekly glance); loses audience identification, since retail-style density is not this operator’s world.
options.risk: Small type tires the eye, and the screen can read as crowded rather than calm.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.thesis: Accounts as rows on a departures board.
options.viewport: A board of account rows with per-character flips.
options.case: Another transit board, black with one amber accent; loses both axes.
options.kept: Columns never move; only values change.
options.risk: Novelty animation on a weekly-glance tool.

options.label: Timetable slide rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight and reversal on raked glass slides.
options.case: Raked containers fight scanning; loses both axes.
options.kept: Exactly one element per screen reverses out.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.thesis: Each page a swelling lobe of flat colour.
options.viewport: One green lobe holding the overview.
options.case: Playful shapes where data needs a grid; loses both axes.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour; no gradients or shadows.

options.label: Convention catalog
options.thesis: Thumbnails keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: Models as a packed thumbnail grid.
options.case: No thumbnails exist to carry it; loses both axes.
options.kept: The list and its home are one space: every name links to where it lives.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern admin dashboard (Linear, Vercel, Cloudflare dashboard), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav; stat cards for requests, failure rate, tokens and accounts; a traffic chart; an accounts table with status badges.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other admin panel by design.
